content.user_title: Instrument Azure Apps with Application Insights
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent telemetry setup for Azure-hosted web applications. This skill gives clear Application Insights guidance for SDK setup, resources, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use auto-instrumentation for Azure App Service apps.
Provides instrumentation references for ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Python, Java, and TypeScript projects.
Shows Bicep and Azure CLI examples for creating Application Insights resources.
Guides configuration of APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING through environment variables and container app secrets.
Includes Container Apps observability guidance, KQL queries, metrics, and Dapr tracing notes.
Links SDK quick references for Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distributions and exporters.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not safely orchestrate project changes by itself.
It assumes access to the target Azure subscription, resource group, and hosted app.
It does not validate live Azure resources or permissions without separate tooling.
Automated implementation may require another skill, such as azure-prepare.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Application Insights instrumentation options for my Azure-hosted web app. Ask for any missing language, framework, or hosting details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan SDK Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan Application Insights SDK setup for my app. Use the correct reference for my language and identify required configuration values.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Azure Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure hosting context and outline the Application Insights and Log Analytics resources I need. Include Bicep or Azure CLI guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review Container Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my Azure Container Apps observability plan. Cover logs, metrics, Application Insights SDK setup, distributed tracing, Dapr, and verification queries.

output_examples.input: A Node.js app runs in Azure App Service and needs request tracing.
output_examples.output: The response identifies manual SDK setup, connection string configuration, deployment timing, and how to verify traces in Application Insights.

output_examples.input: An ASP.NET Core app is hosted in Azure App Service.
output_examples.output: The response explains when portal auto-instrumentation may work and when code-based Azure Monitor setup is needed.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs observability for Azure Container Apps.
output_examples.output: The response covers workspace configuration, app secrets, built-in metrics, console logs, Dapr tracing, and monitoring status checks.

best_practices: Confirm the app language, framework, and Azure hosting model before choosing an instrumentation path.
Store Application Insights connection strings in environment variables or platform secrets, not source files.
Verify telemetry after deployment with Application Map, traces, requests, dependencies, and relevant KQL queries.
anti_patterns: Do not modify appsettings.json for new Application Insights connection string configuration.
Do not add SDK code before environment variables or dotenv configuration are loaded.
Do not use one sampling setting for every workload without considering traffic volume and cost.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance. Use an implementation workflow or another skill when project changes are required.

faq.question: Which hosting platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Azure App Service and Azure Container Apps, with guidance for common web application stacks.

faq.question: Does it support auto-instrumentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when Azure Portal auto-instrumentation can apply to supported App Service applications.

faq.question: How should connection strings be stored?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or Azure platform secrets. Do not commit connection strings into source control.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenTelemetry setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry references for supported languages and exporters.

faq.question: Can it verify telemetry is working?
faq.answer: It provides verification guidance and query examples. Live validation requires access to the target Azure resources.
